# Billing System Migration Rollout Plan
**Scope:** 40,000 existing users | Old and new billing systems run in parallel throughout migration | Target: production start tomorrow

---

## Overview

This migration moves users in controlled batches from the legacy billing system to the new one. Both systems remain live and operational for the entire duration of the rollout — the old system is **not** touched (no disabling, throttling, or decommissioning) until a full validation period after the last user batch has completed successfully.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (Canary)

- **Percentage of users:** 1% (~400 users)
- **Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed staging sign-off, including successful parallel-run reconciliation on synthetic/test accounts for 5 consecutive days with zero critical discrepancies; rollback procedure has been tested end-to-end in staging; on-call rotation is staffed and paged for the pilot window.
- **User selection:** Internal employees + opted-in low-risk customers (no active disputes, standard payment methods only, non-enterprise contracts).
- **Duration:** 3–5 days minimum before proceeding.
- **Focus:** Validate core billing flows (invoicing, payment capture, proration, tax calculation) and data sync accuracy between old and new systems.

## Phase 2: Expanded Rollout

- **Percentage of users:** 25% (~10,000 users, cumulative including Phase 1)
- **Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed its full duration with all exit metrics green (see Halt Metrics below); zero unresolved Sev1/Sev2 billing defects; finance team has manually reconciled a sample of Phase 1 invoices against the old system with matching totals within tolerance.
- **User selection:** Broaden to a representative cross-section of plan types, geographies, and payment methods, still excluding highest-value enterprise accounts.
- **Duration:** 5–7 days minimum.
- **Focus:** Validate at higher concurrency/load, confirm support ticket volume stays within normal bounds, exercise edge cases (refunds, chargebacks, multi-currency).

## Phase 3: General Availability

- **Percentage of users:** 100% (~40,000 users, cumulative)
- **Entry criterion:** Phase 2 completed its full duration with all exit metrics green; support ticket backlog related to billing is at baseline levels; leadership/finance sign-off obtained; final data-consistency audit between old and new systems shows reconciliation variance below threshold (see Halt Metrics).
- **User selection:** All remaining users, migrated in sub-batches (e.g., 10 batches of ~10% each, spaced 12–24 hours apart) rather than a single cutover, to preserve the ability to pause between batches.
- **Duration:** Until last batch completes plus a minimum 14-day stabilization/parallel-run window with both systems live before any discussion of retiring the old system begins as a separate, subsequent project phase.

**Note:** Decommissioning, disabling, or deleting the old billing system is explicitly out of scope for Phase 3 and must be planned as its own later phase, gated on its own entry criteria (minimum 30-day clean parallel run, full audit sign-off, legal/compliance data-retention review).

---

## Halt Metrics (numeric thresholds)

The rollout must be **paused immediately** and the current batch rolled back if any of the following are breached, measured over any rolling 1-hour window during or immediately after a batch:

- **Payment failure rate** on migrated users exceeds **2%** above the pre-migration baseline rate.
- **Billing data reconciliation variance** (dollar-amount mismatch between old and new system ledgers for migrated accounts) exceeds **0.1%** of total billed volume.
- **Critical/Sev1 incident count** related to billing exceeds **2** open at the same time.
- **API error rate** on new billing system endpoints exceeds **1%** over 5-minute intervals, sustained for 15+ minutes.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or double-billing of migrated users due to both systems processing the same invoice cycle | Implement idempotency keys and a migration-status flag per account so only one system is authoritative for billing at any time; add automated duplicate-charge detection with alerting | Billing Platform Engineering Lead
RISK: Data drift between old and new systems causing incorrect balances or invoice history for support agents | Run continuous automated reconciliation jobs comparing account balances every hour during rollout, with alerting on mismatch | Data Integrity / Backend Team Lead
RISK: Payment method or tokenization data fails to migrate correctly, causing failed charges | Pre-validate token migration in a dry run against a payment processor sandbox for 100% of Phase 1 and Phase 2 users before their batch starts; require successful test-charge validation | Payments Integration Lead
RISK: Support team is overwhelmed by billing-related tickets during cutover, delaying issue detection | Staff an elevated on-call and support rotation during each phase window, with a dedicated escalation path and pre-written macros for common migration issues | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Rollback during Phase 3 sub-batches is delayed because migrated users' data has already diverged | Cap batch size and spacing so no more than 10% of users migrate before a rollback checkpoint, and keep the old system fully synced/writable as the system of record until stabilization completes | Program/Release Manager

---

PHASES: 3
